question: A system uses a multilevel feedback queue with 2 queues. Q1: Round Robin, q = 3 ms, highest priority; a process that doesn't finish its time slice moves to the end of Q2. Q2: preemptive SJF. Scheduling between the queues is nonpreemptive priority (a process running from Q2 is not interrupted by arrivals in Q1). All arriving processes enter Q1. What is the sequence of execution?
hint: Track each queue separately and only use Q2 when Q1 is empty.
explanation: P1 runs 3-6 in Q1 (2 ms left -> Q2). P2 arrives at 6 and runs 6-9 in Q1 (1 ms left -> Q2). At 9 Q1 is empty; Q2 has P1 (2) and P2 (1), so SJF runs P2 9-10. P3 arrives at 10 and runs 10-12 in Q1. Finally P1 runs 12-14. Sequence: P1-P2-P3-P1. (Slides 5.25-5.26.)

question: A system uses a multilevel feedback queue with 2 queues. Q1: Round Robin, q = 3 ms, highest priority; a process that doesn't finish its time slice moves to the end of Q2. Q2: nonpreemptive SJF. Scheduling between the queues is preemptive priority; a process preempted from Q2 goes to the end of Q2. All arriving processes enter Q1. A process whose waiting time reaches 8 ms is upgraded to the next higher queue. What is the sequence of execution?
hint: Check the waiting time of the process sitting in Q2 when it may be upgraded.
explanation: Q1: P1 0-3 (3 left -> Q2), P2 3-6 (2 left -> Q2), P3 6-9 (done). At 9 Q2 has P1 (3) and P2 (2): SJF runs P2 9-11. P1 has waited 8 ms (3-11) and is upgraded; it runs 11-14. Sequence: P1-P2-P3-P2-P1. (Slides 5.25-5.26.)

question: A system uses a multilevel feedback queue with 2 queues. Q1: Round Robin, q = 3 ms, highest priority; a process that doesn't finish its time slice moves to the end of Q2. Q2: nonpreemptive SJF. Scheduling between the queues is nonpreemptive priority. All arriving processes enter Q1. A process whose waiting time reaches 7 ms is upgraded to the next higher queue. What is the sequence of execution?
hint: Between-queue scheduling is nonpreemptive, so a Q2 process that has started keeps the CPU.
explanation: P1 runs 0-3 in Q1 (2 left -> Q2). At 3 Q1 is empty, so P1 continues from Q2 3-5 and finishes; P2's arrival at 4 does not preempt it. P2 runs 5-8 in Q1 and finishes, then P3 runs 8-11. Sequence: P1-P2-P3. (Slides 5.25-5.26.)

question: A system uses a multilevel feedback queue with 2 queues. Q1: Round Robin, q = 4 ms, highest priority; a process that doesn't finish its time slice moves to the end of Q2. Q2: nonpreemptive SJF. Scheduling between the queues is nonpreemptive priority. All arriving processes enter Q1. What is the sequence of execution?
hint: When Q1 empties, compare the remaining times in Q2.
explanation: P1 runs 2-6 in Q1 (5 left -> Q2). P2 runs 6-8 in Q1 and finishes. P3 runs 8-12 in Q1 (1 left -> Q2). At 12 Q2 has P1 (5) and P3 (1): SJF runs P3 12-13, then P1 13-18. Sequence: P1-P2-P3-P1. (Slides 5.25-5.26.)

question: A system uses a multilevel feedback queue with 2 queues. Q1: Round Robin, q = 3 ms, highest priority; a process that doesn't finish its time slice moves to the end of Q2. Q2: preemptive priority (a smaller number means a higher priority). Scheduling between the queues is nonpreemptive priority. All arriving processes enter Q1. What is the sequence of execution?
hint: Inside Q2 the smaller priority number wins.
explanation: P1 runs 3-6 in Q1 (2 left -> Q2). P2 runs 6-9 in Q1 (1 left -> Q2). At 9 Q2 has P1 (priority 3) and P2 (priority 2): P2 runs 9-10 and finishes. P3 arrives at 10 and runs 10-13 in Q1 (1 left -> Q2). Q2 now has P1 (3) and P3 (1): P3 runs 13-14, then P1 14-16. Sequence: P1-P2-P3-P1. (Slides 5.25-5.26.)

question: A system uses a multilevel feedback queue with 2 queues. Q1: Round Robin, q = 3 ms, highest priority; a process that doesn't finish its time slice moves to Q2. Q2: nonpreemptive SJF; a process preempted from Q2 goes to the end of Q2. Scheduling between the queues is preemptive priority. All arriving processes enter Q1. A process whose waiting time reaches 4 ms is upgraded to the next higher queue. What is the average waiting time?
hint: An arrival in Q1 preempts a process running from Q2.

question: A system uses a multilevel feedback queue with 2 queues. Q1: Round Robin, q = 2 ms, highest priority; a process that doesn't finish its time slice moves to Q2. Q2: FCFS, lowest priority; a process preempted from Q2 goes to the end of Q2. Scheduling between the queues is preemptive priority. All arriving processes enter Q1. What is the average waiting time?
hint: Each arrival in Q1 interrupts whatever Q2 process is running.
